channel.title: War History Online – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from War History Online – Bias and Credibility (warhistoryonline.com)

item.title: You Won't Believe the Bravery of These 5 Animal Soldiers
item.description: From ammo-carrying bears to spy-hunting dogs, discover the 5 greatest animal war heroes who saved human lives and earned military ranks.

item.title: Ireland’s Secret WWII Bid to Team Up With Germany: Operation Dove
item.description: This St. Patrick’s Day, revisit the shocking true story of how the IRA secretly sought help from Germany during World War II through Operation Dove and covert Abwehr contact.

item.title: Napoleon's Great Example: How Gustavus Adolphus Invented Modern Warfare
item.description: Napoleon considered him one of history's greatest. Discover how Gustavus Adolphus, the Lion of the North, invented mobile artillery and combined arms.

item.title: NATO Troops Are Back in Narvik — The World War II Arctic Battle That Still Feels Urgent
item.description: NATO's Cold Response 2026 exercise has brought 25,000 troops back to Narvik, Norway—the same Arctic port Germany seized in 1940 to control Europe's iron ore supply. Here's why this fjord town matters.

item.title: The Tank Museum Releasing Guide to History's Most Famous Armored Car
item.description: The Daimler Ferret saw over four decades of service across the world.

item.title: The Logistics of Loyalty: Why the Union Wore Blue and the Confederacy Wore Gray
item.description: Why was the Civil War fought in blue and gray? Discover how logistics, chemical dyes, and battlefield confusion shaped the iconic uniforms of the North and South.

item.title: They Fought for a Country That Refused to Fight for Them: The Double V Campaign and America's Segregated WWII Army
item.description: Revisit the Double V Campaign and the segregated WWII U.S. Army, where Black troops fought fascism abroad while facing racism at home.

item.title: Sniper vs Trumpeter: The Normandy Orchard Solo That Stopped a Bullet
item.description: In 1944, a P-47 pilot played a trumpet solo in a dark Normandy orchard. Discover how a German love song stopped a sniper from pulling the trigger.

item.title: March 23, 1943, The Battle of El Guettar: The Day Patton's "Big Red One" Stopped Germany’s Best Tank Corps Dead in Their Tracks
item.description: On March 23, 1943, Patton's forces stopped the 10th Panzer Division cold in the Tunisian desert, marking America's first real victory against German armor in WWII. Here's the story.

item.title: The Last of the Romans: Why Belisarius is the Greatest General You’ve Never Heard Of
item.description: Discover Belisarius, the military genius who reconquered Rome, Africa, and Italy for the Byzantine Empire with a tiny elite force of horse archers.
